content.value_statement: Unfamiliar repositories slow onboarding, reviews, and documentation work. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through structured architecture analysis.
actual_capabilities: Identifies main directories, configuration files, and entry points.
Reviews package, dependency, build, and deployment files.
Maps core modules, services, classes, and responsibilities.
Explains component interactions, APIs, and data flow.
Summarizes deployment setup, environments, and infrastructure signals.
Describes startup flow, request handling, errors, and background work.
limitations: Does not execute code, run tests, or validate runtime behavior.
Does not modify project files or produce implementation changes by default.
Accuracy depends on available files and readable project structure.
Large repositories may need focused follow-up questions.

use_cases.title: Understand a new repository
use_cases.description: Create a clear map of project structure, entry points, components, and runtime flow.

use_cases.title: Draft system documentation
use_cases.description: Turn repository evidence into concise architecture notes and operational explanations.

use_cases.title: Review existing architecture
use_cases.description: Compare modules, dependencies, deployment signals, and service boundaries before planning changes.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Repository Overview
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner scan of an unfamiliar project
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain this codebase at a high level. Cover the main folders, entry points, and major components.

prompt_templates.title: Component Interaction Map
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the core components in this repository. Explain their responsibilities, interfaces, and data flow.

prompt_templates.title: Deployment And Runtime Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this project for deployment architecture and runtime behavior. Include startup flow, environments, dependencies, and error handling.

prompt_templates.title: Full Technical Architecture Brief
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a complete technical architecture brief for this repository. Include structure, dependencies, components, interactions, deployment, and runtime behavior.

output_examples.input: Explain this codebase at a high level.
output: The repository separates application code, tests, configuration, and deployment assets.
The main entry point initializes the server, loads configuration, and registers routes.
Core modules include request handling, persistence, authentication, and background processing.
Deployment files indicate container-based builds with environment-specific configuration.

output_examples.input: How do the main components interact?
output: The API layer receives requests and delegates business operations to service modules.
Services coordinate validation, persistence, and external integrations through defined interfaces.
Data flows from controllers to services, then to storage adapters, with errors returned through shared handlers.

best_practices: Start with repository structure before reading detailed source files.
Use configuration and dependency files to identify frameworks and deployment signals.
Trace runtime flow from entry points through core components.
anti_patterns: Do not treat a single file as the full system design.
Do not recommend implementation changes unless the user asks for them.
Do not skip deployment files when explaining production behavior.

faq.question: What does this skill analyze?
faq.answer: It analyzes repository structure, key files, dependencies, components, interactions, deployment signals, and runtime behavior.

faq.question: Does this skill change my code?
faq.answer: No. It is designed for explanation and documentation, not automatic code modification.

faq.question: Can it work with any programming language?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow is language neutral, but results depend on readable files and recognizable project conventions.

faq.question: Does it run tests or execute the project?
faq.answer: No. It relies on static reading unless the user separately asks for execution.

faq.question: What output should I expect?
faq.answer: Expect a structured technical overview with sections for architecture, components, interactions, deployment, and runtime behavior.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it for onboarding, documentation drafts, architecture reviews, and understanding unfamiliar repositories.
